name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,443

clue.text: Hands pointing to text in square after cubes

indicators.note: after tells us the square's letter comes behind the cubes rather than ahead of them

blocks.note: taken as written
dice are small cubes thrown in games
S is a standard abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: A printer's pointing-hand symbols direct the eye to text inside a box following some cubed figures.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a long phrase: in old printing a little pointing hand (a manicule) drew attention to a line of text.
explanation.definitionFit: An index is the printer's pointing-hand symbol, and indices is its plural, so such marks are literally hands pointing at text.

clue.text: Swallow nesting in charming estuary

indicators.note: something nesting in a phrase sits tucked inside it, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters across the end of charming and the start of estuary

explanation.surface: A swallow builds its nest in a pretty river mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Swallow reads as the bird, helped by nesting, but it is the verb to gulp down.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or drink into the body, which is exactly what swallowing does.

clue.text: Medic leading operation on extremely squidgy swelling

indicators.note: a medic leading means the doctor's letters go in front of what follows
extremely points to the very ends of the next word, keeping only its outermost letters

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
OP is short for a surgical operation
the first and last letters of squidgy

explanation.surface: A doctor about to operate on a soft, squashy swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is the old medical name for oedema, an abnormal swelling of the body caused by fluid build-up.

clue.text: Come across mineral with spiky tip that's awkward to handle

indicators.note: come across is read as come stretched over, so its letters lie either side of what follows
the tip of a word is its leading letter, so only the first letter of spiky is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
umber is a natural brown earth pigment
the first letter of spiky

explanation.surface: Finding a pointed mineral specimen that is difficult to carry.
explanation.walkthrough: Umber is a brown earth used as a pigment, as in burnt umber; come across here is a container, not 'find'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cumbersome is bulky and unwieldy, so it is awkward to carry or manage.

clue.text: Small fruit on small vessels

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above, so the fruit sits on top of the second small

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a hip is the fruit of the rose
S again for small

explanation.surface: Tiny berries placed on little bowls or dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessels looks like containers for the fruit, but it means boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Vessel is a common word for a boat or ship, especially a large seagoing one.

clue.text: Ancient building may drip fluid

indicators.note: fluid means flowing and changeable, so the preceding letters are free to rearrange

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Warning that an old monument might leak water.
explanation.definitionFit: The pyramids of Egypt are among the best-known structures surviving from the ancient world.

clue.text: Heads of physics turned sea creature into remarkable things

indicators.note: heads in the plural means the opening letters of physics are taken, here the first two
turned means flipped round, so the creature's name is read from its end back to its start

blocks.note: the first two letters of physics
a sea anemone is a soft-bodied marine animal

explanation.surface: Senior physicists transformed some marine animal into something astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Heads usually gives one letter; here two letters of physics are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A phenomenon can be an extraordinary person or event, and phenomena are such wonders in the plural.

clue.text: Bachelor leaving food in study

indicators.note: the bachelor leaving means his letter departs from the food word

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor
bread is a staple food

explanation.surface: A single man walks off from his meal while working in his den.
explanation.walkthrough: Study looks like a room, but it is the verb, as in read law at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject is the British way of saying to study it at university.

clue.text: Very old stamp given to five tucking into food

indicators.note: tucking into food means going inside the meal, so these letters are placed within it

blocks.note: a die is a tool for stamping a design onto metal
V is the Roman numeral for five
a meal is a serving of food

explanation.surface: An ancient seal is handed to five people eating dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Stamp is the tool, not the postage: a die is the block that stamps coins and medals.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval means belonging to the Middle Ages, and informally it describes anything hopelessly old-fashioned.

clue.text: Cuckoo seen in borders of desolate wild garden

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its two edges, so only the first and last letters of desolate are kept
wild means out of control, so the letters of the next word run free into a new order

blocks.note: the first and last letters of desolate
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cuckoo is spotted at the edges of an abandoned, overgrown garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuckoo, set beside a garden, wants to be the bird; it is the informal word for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo is informal for mad or crazy, and deranged means mentally unbalanced or insane.

clue.text: Grand space for curry?

blocks.note: G is short for grand, slang for a thousand
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: Asking whether there is plenty of space for a spicy Indian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Curry looks like the dish; it is the verb meaning to brush down a horse, as with a currycomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry a horse is to rub it down with a comb, and to groom one is to brush and clean it.

clue.text: European slipping spirit into fermented cider

indicators.note: slipping something into another means sliding it inside, so the spirit goes within
fermented means worked and changed by yeast, so the drink's letters are churned into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
elan is spirit or verve

explanation.surface: A traveller from the Continent spiking a glass of cider with a shot of liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit suggests a strong drink next to cider; it is the abstract sense, liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: An Icelander is a native of Iceland, a country in northern Europe, so a European.

clue.text: Head of state visiting America given funds for stay

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept from state

blocks.note: the first letter of state
US is short for the United States
a pension is a regular retirement income

explanation.surface: A foreign leader on a trip to the United States receives cash to cover their visit.
explanation.walkthrough: Stay is not a visit here but a halt, as in a stay of execution.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a postponement or halt of proceedings, and a suspension likewise temporarily stops something.

clue.text: Old nurse squeezing opening of wound to be stitched

indicators.note: squeezing something means holding it tight inside, so the nurse's letters surround it
the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken from wound

blocks.note: SEN is State Enrolled Nurse, a British nursing grade now discontinued
the first letter of wound

explanation.surface: A veteran nurse pinches a cut closed so it can be sutured.
explanation.walkthrough: Opening of a wound reads as the cut itself, but it only means its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewn is the past participle of sew, meaning joined with needle and thread, which is what stitched means.

clue.text: Purgatives sorted out males with spots

indicators.note: sorted out means put into a new order, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: part of the letters to be rearranged
the rest of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Laxatives fixed young men with acne.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom salts, magnesium sulphate, have long been taken as a laxative to clear the bowels.

clue.text: Writer drinks fruit smoothie at last

indicators.note: at last means only the final letter of the word before is taken

blocks.note: shakes are milkshakes, thick drinks
a pear is a fruit
the last letter of smoothie

explanation.surface: An author finally drinks a blended fruit smoothie.
explanation.walkthrough: Drinks looks like a verb for the writer's action; it is a noun giving milkshakes.
explanation.definitionFit: William Shakespeare is the most famous English playwright and poet, so he is a writer par excellence.

clue.text: Target for abuse torments topless partner

indicators.note: topless means the head is removed, so the first letter of the torment word goes

blocks.note: to haunt someone is to torment them persistently
an ally is a partner or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone who gets picked on suffers cruelty from a half-naked companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British pub game in which sticks are thrown at a dummy's head, hence a figure everyone attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aunt Sally is a person or idea set up to be criticised, a figurative butt for everyone's attacks.

clue.text: Fish with small sharp extremity almost turned on sailor

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the final letter of the sharp extremity is cut
turned means facing the other way, so the shortened word is read backwards

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a pike is a sharp point, as on a spearhead
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A fish with a little pointed end flips over onto a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: Pike tempts as the fish, but it is the spear point.
explanation.definitionFit: The skipjack is a species of tuna, a fish caught widely for canning.

clue.text: Suspect alarmed by new public official

indicators.note: suspect means dodgy and unreliable, so the next word's letters are not to be trusted in their order

blocks.note: the bulk of the letters to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A suspect frightened by a newly appointed civic dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior elected member of a borough or city council, so a holder of civic office.

clue.text: Brief dispatch by independent fellow before clash on old mountain

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of dispatch's synonym is dropped
before sets the fellow's letters ahead of the clash in the line

blocks.note: to dispatch is to kill
I is the abbreviation for independent
a fellow is a man
to jar is to clash, as colours or sounds do
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A short report from a lone man ahead of a fight on an ancient peak.
explanation.walkthrough: Dispatch reads as a news report, but it means to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilimanjaro, in Tanzania, is the highest mountain in Africa, a dormant volcano.

clue.text: Whale gutted by nasty insect

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters of whale

blocks.note: the first and last letters of whale
evil means wicked or nasty

explanation.surface: A whale is cut open by a horrible bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a small beetle with a long snout, a pest of grain and stored food, so an insect.

clue.text: Lecturer stopping scruffy notes being plagiarised

indicators.note: stopping here means plugging a gap, so the lecturer's letter is lodged inside
scruffy means messy and untidy, so the next word's letters are in disarray

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for lecturer
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tutor stops untidy lecture notes being copied by students.
explanation.definitionFit: Plagiarised work has been taken from someone else and passed off as one's own, so it is stolen.

clue.text: Colourful mixed type

blocks.note: first meaning: patched or blotched in two or more colours, like a magpie
second meaning: printer's type that has been spilt and jumbled together

explanation.walkthrough: Pie is a printing term for a heap of spilt type, and as a verb to pie type is to jumble it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pied describes animals with patches of different colours, and also printing type that has been muddled up.

clue.text: Blockheads dispatched to take first part of maths test

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so dispatched's synonym encloses a letter
the first part of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken from maths

blocks.note: asses are fools
dispatched means sent off
the first letter of maths

explanation.surface: Dunces are sent in to sit the opening paper of a mathematics exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is an evaluation of a student's work or ability, which is what a test is.

clue.text: English book about a way to show one's feelings

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters before it are read from the other end

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: An English book on how to express your emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to display feelings openly or theatrically, especially as an actor does.

clue.text: Lazy brother abandoning check

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the brother's letters are dropped from the check word

blocks.note: BR is the abbreviation for brother
to bridle is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A slothful sibling skips an inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: Check suggests an inspection; here it means to restrain, as a bridle reins in a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle and lazy both describe someone avoiding work or effort, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Animal and a plant enveloped by strange aroma

indicators.note: enveloped by means wrapped up inside, so the plant sits within the other letters
strange means odd and out of the ordinary, so the next word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: dill is an aromatic herb
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A creature and a herb are both surrounded by a peculiar smell.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an American mammal protected by bony armour plates, so an animal.

clue.text: Uniform that's reversible?

indicators.note: reversible means it can be turned back to front and still be the same, which is the hint to the word's shape

blocks.note: the answer reads identically backwards and forwards

explanation.surface: Asks whether a uniform is the kind of garment that can be worn inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversible suggests a jacket worn either way out; it describes a word spelt the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means even and consistent throughout, which is what level means.

clue.text: Clue about points awarded to Democratic president

indicators.note: about means around, so the clue word's letters surround the rest

blocks.note: north-north-east, a point of the compass made of several points
D is the abbreviation for Democratic
a key is a clue to solving something

explanation.surface: A hint about the votes given to a Democrat who occupied the White House.
explanation.walkthrough: Points suggests a score; here it is compass points, north-north-east, which with D sits inside KEY after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: John F. Kennedy was the thirty-fifth US president and a member of the Democratic Party.

clue.text: Letter from Poles in translation

indicators.note: in translation means rendered into another form, so the letters are converted into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A message sent by Polish people, rendered into English.
explanation.walkthrough: Letter looks like correspondence; it is a character of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, corresponding to the short E.
